question: Is there a Limited License for teachers, and when is it used?

input.query: Is there a Limited License for teachers, and when is it used?

answer.summary: Yes. A Limited License is one of the teacher license classifications, and it is a three-year renewable license for an individual who completed an educator preparation program but has not passed the required licensure exam. It can be requested for a teacher employed by a public school unit, and the LICN-023 §1(b) pathway for former lateral-entry license holders applies only if the teacher meets its conditions.

claims.text: A Limited License is one of the teacher license classifications listed in LICN-010 §5(d), as provided in LICN-023.
A Limited License is defined as a three-year renewable license issued to an individual who has completed an EPP but has not satisfied the applicable licensure examination requirements.
A governing body of a public school unit may request a Limited License for an applicant under its employment if the applicant meets the requirements of G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(4a).
A Limited License may only be issued for teaching license areas, not for administrator or student services personnel license areas.

A person who previously held a lateral entry license under G.S. 115C-297 (repealed by S.L. 2017-189), who meets all IPL or CPL requirements except the licensure examination, qualifies for a Limited License if the person is currently employed by the PSU governing body and the PSU submits an affidavit signed by the local superintendent (or equivalent) and the applicant's principal stating the person is employed, is an effective teacher, and the PSU will encourage the applicant to pursue an IPL or CPL.
Limited Licenses are not eligible for added teaching areas (add-ons).

To renew a Limited License, the employing PSU must submit an affidavit signed by the supervising principal and local superintendent attesting that the licensee is currently employed, is an effective teacher, and the PSU will encourage the licensee to pursue a CPL.

To renew a Limited License, the licensee must meet or exceed expected growth as measured by EVAAS where data is available. If more than one year of data exists, DPI averages the growth data. Only data since the license was first issued or last renewed counts, and DPI does not consider 2019-2020 or 2020-2021 EVAAS data.
A Limited License cannot be transferred from one PSU to another, except for military service members and spouses covered by LICN-028.

question: How long is a Residency License valid and can it be extended?

input.query: How long is a Residency License valid and can it be extended?
residency license valid for three years expiration term
residency license duration validity extension renewal limit

answer.summary: A residency license is a one-year license that can be renewed twice, so it runs up to three years in total. Each renewal depends on the employing unit documenting that the applicant meets the renewal conditions, and the license must be converted to an IPL or CPL by June 30 of the third year or it expires.

claims.text: A residency license is a one-year license, renewable twice.
Counting the initial year plus two renewals gives up to three one-year periods, so a residency license can last up to three years in total.

To renew, the employing public school unit or eligible nonpublic school must document that the applicant is enrolled in a recognized educator preparation program, is employed as a teacher there, acquired at least six months of teaching experience during the preceding school year, and completed 10 days of professional development in the first year of the residency license.

If the applicant fails to renew for the second or third year, the residency license expires. The employing unit may request reinstatement if it hires the applicant within three years of the initial residency license's effective date, provided the license has not already been renewed twice and the applicant is enrolled in an educator preparation program.

To avoid expiration, the applicant must meet the IPL or CPL requirements and be recommended by the preparing EPP by June 30 of the third year of the residency license. If met, the IPL or CPL is effective July 1 of the next fiscal year; if not, the residency license expires and the IPL or CPL takes effect when the requirements are later met.

For a servicemember or spouse pursuing a residency license who is called to active duty or relocated outside North Carolina by military orders, the three-year timeframe is held in abeyance until the servicemember returns to North Carolina and returns to employment in a North Carolina public school.
A residency license expires June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire unless it is renewed, extended, or converted under SBE policy.

Did the applicant complete the first-year 10 days of professional development and acquire at least six months of teaching experience in the preceding school year?

The passages do not describe the rules that applied to residency licenses before the current version effective 2026-07-01, so earlier rules cannot be confirmed.

question: What's the process to move from an RL to an IPL?

input.query: What's the process to move from an RL to an IPL?
licensure examination requirements for initial professional license teacher passing score

answer.summary: To convert a residency license (RL) to an initial professional license (IPL), the applicant must meet the LICN-020 IPL requirements and be recommended by the educator preparation program (EPP) that prepared them. If those requirements are met by June 30 of the RL's third year, the IPL takes effect July 1 of the next fiscal year; if not, the RL expires and the IPL takes effect when the requirements are met.

claims.text: To convert a residency license to an IPL or CPL, the applicant must meet the requirements for an IPL in LICN-020 and must be recommended by the EPP that prepared the licensee.

LICN-020 §1 sets out three ways to qualify for an IPL: (a) completing a recognized North Carolina EPP and being recommended by that EPP for the requested license; (b) completing an EPP based outside North Carolina; or (c) holding a clear out-of-state license and having fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction.

If the applicant satisfies the conversion requirements by June 30 of the third year of the residency license, the IPL is effective July 1 of the next fiscal year. If the applicant does not satisfy them by that date, the residency license expires and the IPL is effective on the date the applicant satisfies the requirements.
An IPL entitles the licensee to practice as an independent professional educator in North Carolina.

A residency license is issued to an applicant under the employment of a public school unit or eligible nonpublic school. It requires completing at least 24 hours of coursework in the content area or passing the applicable licensure examination for that area.

LICN-020 §2 allows a public school unit to request an IPL for an applicant who completed all requirements of a recognized North Carolina EPP but has not met the licensure examination requirements, and in that case the EPP recommendation is not required. The passages do not state whether this exception applies when converting a residency license.

question: What are the requirements for a CPL in terms of years of experience and renewal cycle?

input.query: What are the requirements for a CPL in terms of years of experience and renewal cycle?
administrator license years of experience required for continuing professional license

answer.summary: A North Carolina continuing professional license (CPL) is five years renewable under all three role policies. For teachers, the CPL requires at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and out-of-state applicants need more than three years of licensed professional educator experience. The passages set no separate years-of-experience requirement for administrators or student services personnel, so the applicable role determines the answer.

claims.text: A CPL is a five-year, renewable license issued to an applicant or professional educator who meets the relevant requirements established by SBE policy.
A teacher holding a CPL must renew it every five years.
A person holding an administrator license must renew it every five years.
A person holding a student services personnel license must renew it every five years.

To qualify for a continuing professional teacher license, an applicant must hold an initial professional educator license or residency license in North Carolina, and must have at least three years of licensed teaching experience.

A teacher applicant must also complete a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless the applicant has at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina, or previously held a CPL that reverted to an IPL under LICN-030.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a CPL, if the applicant holds a clear license from another jurisdiction and meets the substantially-similar or National Board criteria.

For administrator or student services personnel CPLs, the passages require meeting the examination requirements and the other requirements of LICN-011 or LICN-012, but state no separate minimum years of experience.

Teachers employed by a local board of education must have a rating of at least "proficient" on their most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL, meaning Proficient or higher on three of five Professional Teaching Standards including Standard 4.

Renewal CEU requirements for a teacher in Grades 6 through 12 are eight CEUs per five-year cycle, with four in the license area and four general CEUs. Teachers in Pre-K through Grade 5 must complete eight CEUs per cycle with a different breakdown.

Administrators must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle (four leadership CEUs and four general CEUs), and student services personnel must complete eight CEUs per cycle (four discipline-aligned CEUs and four general CEUs).

question: How many CEUs are needed to renew a CPL, and do any have to be in a specific area?

input.query: How many CEUs are needed to renew a CPL, and do any have to be in a specific area?

answer.summary: A teacher renewing a CPL needs 8 CEUs per five-year cycle, and at least some must be in the teacher's license area. The exact split depends on grade band (PK-5 teachers also need literacy CEUs) and on whether the educator is a teacher, administrator, or student services personnel.

claims.text: A CPL must be renewed every five years, and each teacher holding a CPL must complete CEUs during each renewal cycle.

One CEU equals either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from an institution of higher education, or ten clock hours of professional development programming. So 8 CEUs equal 8 × 10 = 80 clock hours, or 8 × 2/3 = 5 1/3 semester credit hours.

Teachers in Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5 must complete 8 CEUs per renewal cycle: 3 CEUs in the teacher's license area (consistent with Standards 3 and 4), 3 CEUs related to literacy under G.S. 115C-270.30(b)(2), and 2 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Arithmetic: 3 + 3 + 2 = 8.

Teachers in Grades 6 through 12 must complete 8 CEUs per renewal cycle: 4 CEUs in the teacher's license area (consistent with Standards 3 and 4) and 4 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Arithmetic: 4 + 4 = 8. No literacy-specific CEUs are required for this band.

Administrators must complete 8 CEUs per renewal cycle: 4 focused on the administrator's leadership role in instruction, human resources, and management, and 4 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Arithmetic: 4 + 4 = 8.

Student services personnel must complete 8 CEUs per renewal cycle: 4 that align with the North Carolina standards for their professional discipline under the EVAL policy series, and 4 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Arithmetic: 4 + 4 = 8. School audiologists and school speech-language pathologists are exempt from these CEU requirements while they continue to meet LICN-012.

Credit from a National Board for Professional Teaching Standards certification counts for all 8 CEUs in the cycle in which the teacher receives it. Renewing a National Board certification earns 2 CEUs in the renewal cycle in which it is renewed.

Hours in mandatory training programs count toward CEUs only if the training is required by State law or by a local board of education as a condition of employment, and the educator otherwise meets the renewal requirements for the license type.

Each PSU must adopt policies ensuring that renewal activities are appropriate for each educator, considering direct relationship to the educator's work, any school improvement plan, and State Board and DPI strategic priorities. A PSU may also set additional CEU requirements based on local needs.

answer.summary: For a teaching license, an applicant can add a new area to an existing initial (IPL) or continuing (CPL) professional license by passing the NC licensure exam for that area or by completing 24 credit hours of coursework in that area with a C or better in each course. answer.summary: Out-of-state teachers in NC generally enter on an Initial Professional License (IPL) if they have fewer than three years of licensed experience, or on a Continuing Professional License (CPL) if they have more than three years and hold a clear out-of-state license plus either NBPTS certification or substantially similar requirements. Exam timing and the need for NC exams depend on license area and years of experience, so the specific case needs those facts before a determination.

claims.text: An out-of-state applicant with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for an initial professional license (IPL) if they either hold a license in the corresponding license area in another jurisdiction, or completed an educator preparation program recognized by the jurisdiction where that EPP is based.

An out-of-state applicant who qualifies for an IPL in Elementary Education or Special Education: General Curriculum must satisfy the applicable NC licensure exam requirements by the end of the third year of licensure, even if they passed an out-of-state exam in that area.

For an IPL in any other license area, the applicant must either pass an out-of-state exam for that area in the examining jurisdiction, or satisfy the applicable NC exam requirements before or during the third year of licensure, having attempted those exams at least once during the first year.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a CPL if they hold a clear license from another jurisdiction and either hold NBPTS certification or the other jurisdiction's requirements are substantially similar to NC's (at minimum, completion of a recognized EPP and a passing score on an out-of-state exam for each license area sought).

A 'clear license' for CPL purposes is in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, not revoked or disciplined, not subject to a pending unprofessional conduct investigation, and not surrendered while under such investigation in any state.
Evidence of out-of-state exam results must be presented at initial NC licensure, and an out-of-state applicant may not use out-of-state exam results to convert an IPL to a CPL.

An out-of-state applicant who qualifies for a teacher license may add another teaching area based solely on a passing out-of-state exam score in that area if evidence is submitted at the time of initial application. Adding an area after NC licensure is issued falls under LICN-013, which is not in the provided passages.

A separate general route under LICN-020 allows an applicant who holds a clear out-of-state license and has fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction to qualify for an IPL, and LICN-020 also covers applicants who completed an EPP based outside NC.

To move from an IPL to a CPL, the teacher must hold an NC IPL or residency license, satisfy the applicable exam requirements before or during the third year of licensure, have at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and complete a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless they have at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside NC.

Servicemembers and their spouses holding a covered license from another state, relocating to NC on military orders, have that license recognized for the covered license areas upon application with proof of orders, a notarized affidavit, and (for spouses) a marriage certificate. Recognition continues until the later of the order expiration or June 30 of that fiscal year. Out-of-state exam scores for these applicants need not come from the jurisdiction where they completed their EPP.

Application fees in the provided fee schedule (applications opened effective January 1, 2017) are $100 for an out-of-state initial professional license versus $70 for an in-state initial professional license. This schedule is dated 2018-04-05 and may not reflect current fees.

input.query: How much teaching experience counts toward moving up a license level?

answer.summary: The policies set a three-year threshold for the continuing professional license (CPL) but do not say how that threshold is counted. claims.text: To qualify for a continuing professional teacher license, an applicant must hold an initial professional educator license or residency license in North Carolina and have at least three years of licensed teaching experience.

A CPL teacher applicant with at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina is excused from the Beginning Teacher Support Program requirement, but the three-year licensed experience requirement itself still applies as written in §1(c).

An applicant whose license came from another jurisdiction qualifies for an initial professional license only if the applicant holds a clear out-of-state license and has fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction. Otherwise the applicant must have completed an EPP.

Converting a residency license to an IPL or CPL requires meeting the IPL or CPL requirements and an EPP recommendation. If the requirements are met by June 30 of the residency license's third year, the conversion takes effect July 1 of the next fiscal year.

Renewing a residency license requires documentation that the applicant acquired at least six months of teaching experience during the preceding school year. This is a renewal condition, not a CPL experience threshold.

For salary experience credit, one year is earned for full-time work of at least six calendar months within one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30). Part-time work must be at least 15 hours per week to count, and partial years can be combined into one year of credit.

Service as a tutor, clerical paraprofessional, or substitute teacher is not recognized as professional educator experience credit for salary purposes. Time on approved leave of absence is also excluded.

Under the policies provided, the three-year CPL requirement is stated as 'licensed teaching experience,' but the policies provided do not define that term or say whether salary experience credit, part-time work, or substitute work counts toward it.

A permit to teach cannot be extended or renewed and is valid only until June 30 of the fiscal year requested. A residency license holder cannot later hold a permit or emergency license in the same area.

claims.text: The renewal minimum for teachers is 8 CEUs per five-year renewal cycle, whether the teacher teaches Pre-K through Grade 5 or Grades 6 through 12.

A CEU is either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from an institution of higher education or ten clock hours of professional development programming. At 10.0 CEUs, the teacher has 10 − 8 = 2.0 CEUs above the minimum. If all 10.0 CEUs were clock-hour programming, that is 10 × 10 = 100 clock hours; if they were college credit, that is 10 × (2/3) ≈ 6.67 semester credit hours.

For a Pre-K through Grade 5 teacher, the 8 CEUs must include 3 in the license area, 3 literacy CEUs, and 2 general CEUs. The 10.0 total only satisfies the requirement if these category minimums are also met.
For a Grade 6 through 12 teacher, the 8 CEUs must include 4 in the license area and 4 general CEUs. The 10.0 total only satisfies the requirement if these category minimums are also met.

A teacher employed by a local board must have evidence of a rating of at least "proficient" on the most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL. That means "Proficient" or higher on three of the five NC Professional Teaching Standards, including "Proficient" on Standard 4.

If the teacher was not deemed proficient, and is in the final year of a cycle with a current CPL, the LSAU may place them on a mandatory improvement plan (IPL), and the license then reverts to an IPL. Without such a plan, the license expires at the end of the cycle.
Mandatory training hours count toward CEUs only if the training is required by State law or by a local board as a condition of employment, and the teacher has otherwise met the renewal requirements.
A National Board Certified teacher receives credit for all 8 CEUs in the year of certification, and 2 CEUs in the cycle in which the certification is renewed.

claims.text: LICN-020 §1(c) allows an applicant who holds a clear license from another jurisdiction to qualify for an initial professional license only if the applicant has fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction.

LICN-025 §2 allows an out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience to qualify for a continuing professional license, provided both §2(a) and §2(b) are met.

Under LICN-025 §2(a), a clear license must be in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, not revoked or disciplined, free of any pending unprofessional-conduct investigation, and not voluntarily surrendered during an investigation. A valid license alone does not establish that it is clear.

Under LICN-025 §2(b), the applicant must either hold NBPTS certification or come from a jurisdiction whose requirements are substantially similar to NC's. Substantially similar means the jurisdiction required, at minimum, completion of a recognized EPP and a passing score on an out-of-state exam for each license area sought.
Under LICN-025 §3, evidence of out-of-state exam results must be presented at the time of initial NC licensure, and out-of-state exam results cannot be used to convert an IPL to a CPL.

LICN-025 §1(a) uses the term 'licensed professional educator experience' and LICN-025 §2 uses 'more than three years of licensed professional educator experience.' LICN-006 §I governs experience credit for salary purposes for NC public school employees. It is not stated in the passages as the rule for licensure eligibility, so it cannot be used to determine how many years count toward the NC license.

Under LICN-024 §1(d)(i), the Beginning Teacher Support Program requirement for a CPL is waived for applicants with at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina. That policy governs CPL applicants who hold an NC IPL or residency license, so its application to a direct out-of-state CPL is not addressed in the passages.

question: Teacher wants to know if 0.5 CEU from a conference counts. Conference was 4 hours long. Does one CEU equal 10 hours or something else?

answer.summary: Under the clock-hour definition, a 4-hour conference is worth 0.4 CEU, not 0.5 CEU. A 0.5 CEU value would only fit if the conference were college credit, which the analyst has not indicated, and the employing PSU must still accept the activity under its own criteria.

claims.text: One CEU is defined as either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from an institution of higher education, or ten clock hours of professional development programming.
Under the clock-hour definition, 4 clock hours is 4 ÷ 10 = 0.4 CEU, so a 4-hour conference does not produce 0.5 CEU.

Under the college-credit definition, 0.5 CEU would equal 0.5 ÷ (2/3) = 0.75 semester credit hour, so a conference could yield 0.5 CEU only if it were college credit worth 0.75 semester credit hour. The passages do not say the conference was for college credit.

claims.text: A CEU is either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from an institution of higher education or ten clock hours of professional development programming.

If a teacher employed by a local board is in the final year of a renewal cycle and was not deemed proficient, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan. If the teacher is placed on the plan and otherwise meets requirements, DPI issues an IPL. If the teacher is not placed on the plan, the license expires at the end of the renewal cycle.
A General Assembly member is exempt from the continuing education requirements for any cycle in which they serve, if they notify DPI of the exemption during that cycle.
A school audiologist or school speech-language pathologist is exempt from the student services continuing education requirements while they continue to meet LICN-012.

A teacher who receives National Board Certification receives credit for all eight CEUs for the cycle in which it is received. A teacher who renews National Board Certification receives credit for two CEUs for the cycle of renewal.

question: Teacher earned NBPTS certification in 2019. License expires next year. Does the national board cert affect renewal?

answer.summary: The NBPTS certification only gives CEU credit in the renewal cycle in which it was received or renewed, so the 2019 date matters only if it falls inside the teacher's current five-year cycle. claims.text: A teacher who receives National Board Certification gets credit for all eight CEUs for the renewal cycle in which the certification is received.
A teacher who renews National Board Certification gets credit for two CEUs for the renewal cycle in which the certification is renewed.
A renewal cycle is the five-year period between each renewal of a CPL, so a 2019 receipt counts toward the current cycle only if the current cycle began on or before 2019 and runs past it.

Each teacher holding a CPL must renew every five years and complete eight CEUs per cycle. Grades 6-12 teachers complete four CEUs in the license area and four general CEUs; PreK-5 teachers complete three license-area, three literacy, and two general CEUs.

One CEU equals either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from a higher education institution or ten clock hours of professional development. The NB credit is stated directly in CEUs, so no conversion is needed.

Teachers employed by a local board must have a rating of at least proficient on the most recent annual evaluation (proficient on three of five standards, including Standard 4) to renew a CPL. The passages do not say that NB certification waives this requirement.

If the teacher is not rated proficient and is in the final year of the cycle, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan, which leads to an IPL; otherwise the license expires at the end of the cycle.
Licenses expire on June 30 of the year they are set to expire unless renewed, extended, or converted.

question: Applicant from Georgia, 2 years of teaching, needs NC license. What do they qualify for?
context_ids: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

input.query: Applicant from Georgia, 2 years of teaching, needs NC license. What do they qualify for?

answer.summary: Based on two years of licensed teaching experience, this out-of-state applicant can qualify for an NC Initial Professional License (IPL), not a Continuing Professional License, provided they meet either the Georgia license-in-area or recognized-EPP route. The IPL is three years and nonrenewable, and the examination deadline depends on the license area and whether a passing Georgia exam score exists, so the analyst needs the facts listed in questions_for_user before confirming.

claims.text: An out-of-state applicant with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for an initial professional license (IPL).

To qualify for that IPL, the applicant must either hold a license in the corresponding license area in a jurisdiction outside North Carolina, or have completed an educator preparation program recognized by the jurisdiction where the EPP has its principal place of business.
Georgia is a jurisdiction outside North Carolina, and an out-of-state applicant is one who completed an EPP or APP with a principal place of business outside North Carolina.
An IPL is a three-year, nonrenewable license.
An applicant who completed an EPP based outside North Carolina may qualify for an IPL under the general initial license rule.
An applicant holding a clear license from another jurisdiction with fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience there may also qualify for an IPL under the general initial license rule.
Two years of experience counts toward the three-year threshold only if it is licensed professional educator experience.

For an IPL in Elementary Education or Special Education: General Curriculum, the applicant must satisfy the applicable NC licensure examination requirements by the end of the third year of licensure, regardless of any out-of-state exam result.

For an IPL in any other license area, the applicant must either achieve a passing score on an out-of-state exam for that area in the examining jurisdiction, or satisfy the NC examination requirements before or during the third year, having attempted the NC exams at least once during the first year.
A CPL based on out-of-state licensure requires more than three years of licensed professional educator experience, so two years does not qualify for a CPL under that route now.
An out-of-state exam result cannot be used to convert an IPL to a CPL; NC examination requirements must be satisfied, and out-of-state exam evidence must be presented at initial licensure.

To move from an NC IPL to a CPL, the applicant needs three years of licensed teaching experience, must satisfy the examination requirements before or during the third year, and must complete a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless they have at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina.

The fee schedule lists $100 for an out-of-state initial professional license application opened by an individual educator; this schedule is dated 2018-04-05 and the provided materials do not confirm whether it is current.
citations: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

Does the applicant hold a current Georgia educator license in that same license area, and is it a clear license (in good standing, with no pending investigation, discipline, or surrender)?

Current fee amounts; the fee table provided is dated 2018 and may be outdated.

To add a teaching area, the applicant must either satisfy the applicable licensure examination requirements for that area, or complete 24 credit hours of coursework from an institution of higher education in that area with a grade of C or better in each course.

Exceptional Children: General Curriculum (Kindergarten through Grade 12) is a recognized teacher license classification.

question: Teacher's CPL lapsed three years ago. Taught four years before that. What's the reinstatement process?

input.query: Teacher's CPL lapsed three years ago. Taught four years before that. What's the reinstatement process?
expired continuing professional license reinstatement after lapse, reapply, initial professional license

answer.summary: The policies provided do not describe a general reinstatement process for a lapsed (expired, not revoked) CPL. The likely paths are a PSU-requested validation under LICN-033 §3, which depends on whether the teacher was employed by any PSU in the preceding fiscal year and is employed by the requesting PSU now, or, if the license was revoked rather than lapsed, a petition under LICN-007 §8.

claims.text: LICN-030 §2(b)(iv) says a teacher who meets the renewal criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan has the license expire at the end of the renewal cycle, and may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving notice of expiration from DPI. The policy gives no time limit on that application window, so the passages cannot confirm whether it is still open three years after the lapse.

LICN-033 §3 allows the governing body of a PSU to request that DPI validate an expired CPL for an applicant employed under that PSU, even without the required CEUs, but only if the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year.

A validated CPL is effective for three years. To renew it for a new five-year cycle, the educator must complete the relevant renewal requirements in LICN-030, LICN-031, or LICN-032 by the end of the third year.

LICN-007 §8 covers reinstatement only for a license that was revoked or an application that was denied. A petition may be filed no sooner than 12 months after the effective date of revocation or denial, in writing to the Superintendent, and the Superintendent may deny it, grant it, or grant it on probation.

Renewal of a teacher CPL requires eight CEUs per five-year cycle (for Grades 6-12: four in the license area and four general CEUs), plus evidence of at least a 'proficient' rating on the most recent annual evaluation.
Under LICN-033 §1 and §5, CEUs may be earned through college credit or professional development programs, and PSUs must apply criteria for the appropriateness of activities.

questions_for_user: Did the CPL lapse because it expired at the end of a renewal cycle, or was it revoked? If revoked, when was the revocation effective?
Is the teacher employed by a North Carolina PSU now? Would that PSU's governing body request validation under LICN-033 §3?

Was the teacher employed by any PSU during the fiscal year immediately before the validation request? The four years of teaching are described as before the lapse, so what was the teacher's employment status during the three years since?
Did DPI send the teacher a notice of expiration, and when? This affects the 30-day IPL application window in LICN-030 §2(b)(iv).
Which license area and grade band did the teacher hold (for example, Grades 6-12 or a non-teaching role such as administrator or student services)? This determines which renewal requirements apply.
Did the teacher receive a 'proficient' rating on the most recent annual evaluation, and did the teacher have a mandatory improvement plan?
not_covered: A general reinstatement process for an expired or lapsed (non-revoked) CPL.
Whether the 30-day IPL application window in LICN-030 §2(b)(iv) remains open after a lapse of three years.
Application forms, fees, or documentation requirements for validation under LICN-033 §3 or for an IPL.

Whether the four years of prior teaching experience affect eligibility for an IPL or validation. LICN-024 §1(c) relates to experience for a CPL, but the passages do not say how prior experience applies after a lapse.
Rules in effect before 2026-07-01. The policies provided are current versions only and cannot confirm what applied at the time of the lapse three years ago.

metrics.judge_rationale: The answer gets the central point right: no general reinstatement process exists for a lapsed CPL, and validation under LICN-033 §3 is the main route, with the IPL route and the 12-month petition correctly limited to revoked or denied cases. It omits that a CPL requires a current IPL or residency license first, which matters for this teacher, and it leaves out the June 30 expiration rule and the CEU definition. Its claims are all supported by the cited text.

claims.text: LICN-025 is the policy for individuals holding a professional educator license in another jurisdiction who seek a North Carolina license.
An out-of-state applicant is one who completed an educator preparation program with a principal place of business outside North Carolina.

An out-of-state applicant with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for an IPL if they hold a license in the corresponding license area in another jurisdiction, or completed an EPP recognized by the jurisdiction where that EPP is based.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed experience may qualify for a CPL only if they hold a clear license from another jurisdiction and either hold National Board certification or meet licensure requirements substantially similar to North Carolina's (EPP completion and a passing out-of-state exam in each license area sought).

Under LICN-025, a clear license must be in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, not revoked or disciplined, not subject to a pending unprofessional-conduct investigation, and not surrendered under investigation. The passages do not say expressly whether a license that expired in 2016 meets the renewable criterion or how an expired license is treated.
The Georgia license issued in 2008 and expired in 2016 must be assessed against the clear-license criteria, so the applicant's current licensing status matters for the CPL route.

An out-of-state applicant who qualifies for an IPL in Elementary Education or Special Education: General Curriculum must satisfy NC exam requirements by the end of the third year of licensure. Other areas require either a passing out-of-state exam score or NC exam requirements taken before or during the third year, with an attempt in the first year.
Out-of-state exam results must be presented at initial NC licensure, and an out-of-state applicant may not use out-of-state exam results to convert an IPL to a CPL.

Under LICN-024, a CPL based on an out-of-state clear license must meet LICN-025. Applicants with at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina are exempt from the Beginning Teacher Support Program requirement.
An IPL entitles the licensee to practice as an independent professional educator in North Carolina, and a CPL does the same.
For any license requiring an EPP, the EPP must be recognized by the SBE or by the equivalent licensing authority in the jurisdiction where the EPP has its principal place of business.

The policies provided are the current versions, effective 2026-07-01 for LICN-001, LICN-020, LICN-024, and LICN-025, and as of 2026-10-10. They cannot confirm which versions applied to an application submitted in 2024.

A complete application for most licensure services, other than renewal, must be submitted by April 15 of a fiscal year to guarantee processing before the fiscal year ends. Its effect on a 2024 application cannot be confirmed from the provided versions.
The LICN-008 fee schedule lists $100 for an out-of-state IPL opened by an individual educator, but that schedule is effective 2018-04-05 and its applicability to a 2024 application is not confirmed.
